{
  "need": "Autonomy",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status", "note": "Every excuse is also a bid to be seen as someone who can manage their own life — blowing curfew is partly about proving they are not a kid who gets told when to come home." },
  "read": "They are testing the boundary because that is developmentally on-brand, but three rounds of slippage tells you the current deal feels imposed rather than agreed to. The curfew probably feels like a leash, not a standard, and each time you reset it without a real renegotiation, the implicit message is that the rule is negotiable if they push long enough.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lock it down hard, add punishment, take away privileges — feels decisive but lands as a power move, which triggers more resistance and more creative excuse-making because now it is a contest of wills." },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the pattern out loud without anger, state that the curfew itself is not going away, and then genuinely hand them the wheel on how they earn a later one — so the standard stays firm but the path to more freedom is in their hands, not yours.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "There is a curfew and it will be honored, full stop — this is a safety and trust issue, not a preference.",
    "Missing it without prior contact is a breach of trust, and trust has a cost when it breaks — that consequence stays on the table every time."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "What that curfew actually is can be earned upward over time through a track record they build.",
    "How they check in — text, call, location share — is something they can propose, as long as you actually hear from them.",
    "A one-off late night for something real can be negotiated in advance, never retroactively excused."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I am not coming at you mad, but I do need us to actually talk about this, not just reset the clock again and pretend it is handled. I want us to land somewhere real." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Help me understand what keeps happening. Is the time just unrealistic for how your nights actually go? Is it awkward to leave when everyone else is still there? I am asking because I genuinely want to know, not to catch you in something." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is where I stand: the curfew is not going anywhere because it is about knowing you are safe and being able to trust you. But I am not married to the exact time forever. What would make this actually workable for you — and what would you be willing to do so I feel good about loosening it?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to a curfew because I have high standards for how we treat each other's trust in this family, and I genuinely believe you are capable of meeting them — I have watched you be responsible in harder situations than this. So let's agree right now on the time, on what happens when you are running late, and on what earning a later curfew actually looks like. I need you to help me build that map, because the old one clearly is not working." }
  ],
  "longGame": "The goal is not a kid who sneaks in quietly — it is a young adult who can negotiate, follow through, and self-regulate when no one is watching. Every time they honor the agreement they set with you, flag it specifically and let the curfew inch later; that feedback loop teaches them that their choices have real leverage, which is the whole point."
}
situation: Curfew keeps slipping later and the excuses pile up. We have already reset it twice.
